screen.title: Servers
screen.lead: Run bigger, multi-machine labs on hardware you own. Proxmox or ESXi, over your network.
screen.noServerHint: No server? If this machine can handle it, install a local hypervisor and run VM labs here.
screen.listFailed: Couldn't read your saved servers and cloud accounts
screen.removeBody: Cyber CTF forgets this server and deletes its password from the keychain. Nothing changes on the server itself.

setup.leadCloud: Run labs as throwaway instances in your own cloud account. Credentials stay on this machine, never with Cyber CTF.
setup.leadServer: Point the launcher at your server. The password goes to your OS keychain, never to Cyber CTF.

tools.ovftoolRosetta: Found at {path}, but it's built for Intel Macs: install Rosetta (softwareupdate --install-rosetta), then check again.

tools.placed: OVF Tool copied into Cyber CTF's tools folder: {path}

refused.noTool: There's no ovftool program in that folder. Choose the folder the download unpacked to, the one holding ovftool.
refused.noLibraries: That folder has ovftool but not its lib folder. Choose the whole unpacked folder.
refused.tooLarge: That folder holds far more than the OVF Tool. Choose the folder the download unpacked to.
refused.unsigned: macOS says it isn't validly signed ({detail}). Download it again from Broadcom.
refused.notVmware: It's signed by team {team}, not by VMware (EG7KH642X6), so it wasn't used.
refused.notVmwareUnknown: It isn't signed by VMware (EG7KH642X6), so it wasn't used.

server.title: Your {kind} server
server.description: Where the server is. How the launcher signs in to it comes next.

connection.title: Connect to {kind}
connection.descriptionSsh: The launcher drives the host over SSH.
connection.name: Name
connection.authorizeKeyBody: Token hosts use this key over SSH to upload the cloud-init snippet. Add it to the token user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the Proxmox node.
connection.descriptionSignIn: Choose how the launcher signs in to the Proxmox node.
connection.sshKeyPathHint: Only its path is saved, never the key itself
connection.sshKeyNoteTitle: What the launcher does with your key
connection.sshKeyNoteBody: When you continue, it signs in to the node over SSH with this key, creates an API token for itself with pveum user token add and adds its own public key to the user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. Nothing else runs on the node; labs then use that token.
connection.tokenIdHint: root!name, or user@realm!name (@pam is added when you give no realm)
connection.usernameHintPassword: root, or user@realm (@pam is added when you give no realm)

account.title: How to connect
account.description: Choose how the launcher signs in to AWS.
account.billing: Labs run in your account and are billed while they run; the cost depends on each lab's size. Stopping a lab, or its auto-stop, destroys what it created.
account.cliNote: Sign in with the browser (aws login), or use a profile. No secret stored.
account.keysNote: Or paste an IAM user's key and secret.

descriptions.azure: Sign in with the Azure CLI, then pick your subscription and location.
descriptions.gcp: Sign in with the gcloud CLI, then pick a billing account. Labs run in one Cyber CTF labs project, created on the first test (it needs one free project slot on the billing account).
descriptions.token: Paste a {cloud} API token with read/write scope, and pick a region.
descriptions.oci: Uses ~/.oci/config (API signing key). Pick a compartment and region.
descriptions.awsCli: Sign in with the browser, or pick a profile that's already signed in.

credentials.ociMissing: No ~/.oci/config found. Set it up with `oci setup config` or from the console.
credentials.signedInAzure: Signed in to the Azure CLI.
credentials.azureSignInHint: Sign in with the Azure CLI to list your subscriptions.
credentials.gcpReadFailed: Couldn't read the Google Cloud account: {error}
credentials.billingHint: the labs project is billed here
credentials.billingNone: none listed for this account; type the id
credentials.gcpSignInHint: Sign in with the gcloud CLI to list your billing accounts.
credentials.notSignedInProfile: Not signed in on this profile.
credentials.browserSignIn: Sign in with the browser (aws login)
credentials.accessKeyHint: An IAM user with EC2 access
credentials.createKeys: Create them in the AWS console
credentials.awsCliTooOld: Your AWS CLI is {version}: signing in with the browser (aws login) needs 2.32 or later. Update it, then check again. A profile that's already signed in works meanwhile, or go back and use access keys.
credentials.awsCliUpdate: How to update the AWS CLI

options.otherAutoStop: At the auto-stop time the launcher tears the lab down to end billing, so keep it open (or stop the lab yourself) before then.
options.costNote: Each lab picks its own instance size, so the cost depends on the lab.
